text:
alex_acme: hey team — running into weird behavior with your SSE stream this morning. Our client sees duplicated events after a token refresh/reconnect and sometimes gets a truncated payload. Repro is consistent: initial stream starts, we rotate auth token mid-stream, client reconnects and then receives the last event twice (one partial then full).

maria: thanks for reporting — can you paste the request_id / trace id and the endpoint + model? Also are you on Hosted/Dedicated/Private?

alex_acme: request_id=rs-20260315-8f3b, endpoint=/v1/stream, model=redwood-rlm-13b, deployment=Private (ALB in front of our VPC). Token refresh flow: we rotate bearer token every 10m. Repro steps below — I can also attach pcap.

sophie: do you see any 401/403s or explicit auth retry logs server-side when this happens? Also do you include Last-Event-ID on reconnect or are you starting a fresh GET?

alex_acme: no 401/403 in our app logs; client just closes and re-GETs with the new token. We don't set Last-Event-ID. pcap attached but here's an excerpt of what we see client-side: 

```
FIN from client
Server sends: event: message
id: 123
data: {"chunk":"..."}

new GET (new token) 80ms later
Server: event: message
id: 123
data: {"chunk":"...complete"}

Client gets both -> dedupe needed or server shouldn't replay
```

raj: quick thought — if the client closes the TCP connection while the server still has buffered SSE frames not yet flushed to the wire, an immediate new connection could see retried frames if the proxy/ALB replays buffered output. Do you have ALB idle timeout or keepalive settings tuned? ALB default is 60s.

tim: we also saw a potential corner in our runtime where buffered frames that haven't been acked could end up being replayed when a new accept happens for the same logical session id. Usually SSE is stateless, but when a client reconnects quickly and the load-balancer hands traffic to a new backend process, we've seen double-delivery if last_event_id isn't used to dedupe. Can you share server-side trace id from the original request?

alex_acme: trace_id=tr-98765 and I also captured some server logs around the window. Paste of relevant server logs: 

```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] conn_id=42 accept path=/v1/stream client=10.1.2.3 trace=tr-98765 event=send seq=120 status=200
[2026-03-15T09:12:04Z] conn_id=42 flush queued=3 bytes=1580
[2026-03-15T09:12:04Z] conn_id=42 read error=EOF
[2026-03-15T09:12:04Z] conn_id=43 accept path=/v1/stream client=10.1.2.3 trace=tr-98766 event=auth-check status=200
[2026-03-15T09:12:05Z] conn_id=43 replayed_buffered id=123 bytes=420
```

raj: that "replayed_buffered" line is interesting — suggests buffer wasn't cleared on EOF and new accept drained it again. What ALB config? Are you using HTTP/1.1 keepalive or HTTP/2?

alex_acme: ALB TCP proxy + HTTP/1.1 keepalive disabled, so clients open new TCP connections.

sophie: two parallel asks: 1) can you attach the pcap/gzip and server debug logs for the timeframe? 2) try a quick client-side dedupe by event id (if id present) as workaround. We'll also check runtime's event id sticky behavior.

ingest-bot: deploy completed: runtime v3.14.2 -> health OK (no global alerts) :white_check_mark:

tim: i'm going to dig into the runtime side. Hypothesis: when auth rotates mid-stream we sometimes accept a new connection and the runtime will attempt to flush remaining buffers from a now-closed conn (race). If the new request doesn't include Last-Event-ID we may retry send the same event id. We should either 1) honor Last-Event-ID and skip replayed frames, or 2) ensure buffered frames are cleared on EOF prior to new accept.

raj: for reproducing locally we can simulate token rotation + reconnection. minimal repro: open SSE with token A, after 700ms send a partial chunk (simulate long generator), then kill socket, immediately open new SSE with token B and check for duplicate id. I'll add a curl/socat snippet.

```
# repro (client side, rough)
echo -e "GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nAccept: text/event-stream\r\nAuthorization: Bearer $TOKEN_A\r\n\r\n" | nc $HOST $PORT
# let server send partial
sleep 0.7
# close and reopen with new token
# new GET with TOKEN_B
```

alex_acme: here's a more concrete curl flow that reproduced it for us: 
```
TOKEN_A=xxx
TOKEN_B=yyy
curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN_A" -N "https://redwood.example.com/v1/stream?prompt=test" &
# let it stream for 1s
sleep 1
# rotate token in our auth server
# open new client
curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN_B" -N "https://redwood.example.com/v1/stream?prompt=test"
```

maria: ok we'll file an internal incident ticket and escalate to eng-runtime. Can we get permission to share the pcap and server logs with eng team? Alex, do you consent?

alex_acme: yes please share, we want a fix. attaching pcap in the ticket.

sophie: plan for now: 1) support will add client-side dedupe note in our help doc, 2) eng-runtime will add a guard to clear buffered frames on connection EOF and check last_event_id header on new connects to avoid re-sending identical ids, 3) add metric: sse.duplicate_events.count and alert if >0.5% of streams in 5m window.

tim: i'll own the runtime patch. immediate mitigation: server will honor Last-Event-ID and drop matching buffered frames; longer-term add explicit flush-on-close. I'll open PR and link to ticket.

raj: also add an integration test that simulates mid-stream auth rotation and validates no duplicate ids observed.

alex_acme: thanks everyone — attaching logs + pcap to the ticket now. We'll test the client dedupe in the meantime. Appreciate quick triage. :pray:

maria: creating P2 incident now and assigning to eng-runtime + SRE. Meeting set for 10:30 to triage; i'll drop link in the ticket. :calendar:
